## What is shared, and what is per bench {#sec-bom-shared}

Not everything on this list needs to be bought once per bench. A signal
generator, a digital multimeter and a reference thermometer are each used
for a session at a time, not continuously, and a lab equipping several
benches can share a smaller pool of these across them — which is what
actually sets the cost of equipping a room rather than a single bench. What
does need to be per-bench is anything a student needs continuously through
a session: the board itself, the conditioning and filter boards once built,
and the beam rig if a session runs strain, displacement and vibration back
to back.

## Sourcing criteria {#sec-bom-sourcing}

Not vendors or part numbers — what to check on a datasheet before choosing
one.

- **Voltage reference.** Initial accuracy (ppm), temperature coefficient
  (ppm/°C over the bench's operating range), output noise, and load
  regulation against the current the divider and conditioning stage
  actually draw from it.
- **Instrumentation amplifier.** Gain accuracy and drift against the gain
  the [conditioning board](conditioning-board.qmd#sec-cond-inamp) needs,
  CMRR and how it degrades with frequency, input bias current against the
  source impedance it will see, input offset voltage and drift small
  compared with the smallest signal to resolve, single-supply operation with
  adequate output swing.
- **Strain gauges.** Gauge factor and its tolerance, resistance matched to
  the bridge and amplifier design, a backing material whose thermal
  expansion is compatible with — ideally self-compensated for — whichever
  beam material is chosen in [Beam rig](beam-rig.qmd), a gauge length short
  compared with the strain gradient described in [Beam rig §the
  relations](beam-rig.qmd#sec-beam-relations), and a maximum elongation
  rating well above the working strain.
